Subject: Dedicated capacity options & sizing — PulseCare follow-up

Hi Pete / Lori,

Thanks again for the demo earlier — great to see the inference patterns for your triage assistant. As promised, attached are three capacity options tailored to the usage profile you shared and the 99th-percentile latency targets (<= 350ms for short chat flows). High-level options below; full pricing and the usage spreadsheet are attached.

Option A — Pilot (low-friction)
- Initial cluster: 8 x A100-equivalent GPUs (single pool)
- Minimum reserved: 2 GPUs (to cover baseline inference)
- Ramp: 4 weeks to baseline, 6 weeks to steady production
- Typical throughput: ~120 qps (short prompts), optimized for latency
- Use case: onboarding, lightweight evaluation, early burst testing
- Price: monthly reserved + overage at hosted rate (see PDF)

Option B — Production (recommended for launch)
- Initial cluster: 32 x A100-equivalent GPUs (sharded across two availability zones)
- Minimum reserved: 8 GPUs
- Ramp: 6 weeks to baseline, 12 weeks to full capacity (staged activation)
- Throughput: ~480 qps with KV-cache warmup and batching
- Includes canary routing and warm standby for regional failover

Option C — Peak (enterprise throughput + burst)
- Initial cluster: 64 x mixed T4/A100-equivalents (capacity ladder)
- Minimum reserved: 16 GPUs
- Ramp: 8–16 weeks with staged tranche activations
- Supports sustained peak and predictable burst windows

Notes and assumptions:
- Min reserved GPUs are billed as committed capacity; burst above reserved will use shared excess capacity with priority-based routing.
- We recommend Option B if you plan to move to GA within 2–3 months; Option A is best for a tactical pilot.
- We can accelerate ramp by pre-warming models and moving from single-az to dual-az sooner (impact on price / lead time in attachment).

Next steps:
1) Which option best matches your timeline (Pilot / Production / Peak)?
2) If Production, confirm target GA date so we can finalize the staged ramp and activation windows.
3) I can share a DocuSign with the draft reservation terms and the standard SLA once you pick an option.

Attachments: PulseCare_dedicated_options_v1.pdf, usage-estimates-pulsecare.csv

Thanks — happy to jump on another call to walk through the cost delta between reserved vs burst lanes.

—
Soojin Lee
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
soojin.lee@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0198

Thanks Soojin — helpful overview. A few quick clarifications: 
1) For Option B, the min reserved 8 GPUs — is that per AZ or total? We need to understand availability implications.
2) What's the SLA credit if we hit a regional outage and we failover to the warm standby?
3) For pilots, can we run the model quantized on the pilot GPUs to reduce cost, or do you require full fp16 images for consistency with production?

Also looping in procurement (procurement@pulsecare.io) since we might need standard T&Cs.

—Pete

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Pete Holloway <pete@pulsecare.io>, Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>, Lori Bennett <lori@pulsecare.io>
Date: 2026-10-29T11:17:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity options & sizing — technical clarifications

Hey all — quick answers to Pete's technicals: 
1) Minimum reserved numbers are totals across the account (not per AZ). For HA we recommend we hold the min across two AZs as 8 total (e.g., 4 + 4 warm). If you need firm per-AZ guarantees we can set a floor per-AZ but that increases reserved units.
2) SLA: our Dedicated SLA provides regional uptime commitments; for failovers into the warm-standby we offer a staged credit. Typical wording: 10% monthly service credit for sustained regional loss > 4 hours, escalating for longer outages (full terms in the attached PDF). We can escalate exceptions for enterprise customers with a stronger credit table if needed.
3) Pilot quantization: yes — we support INT8/Q4 quantized variants on pilot pools. The caveat is that some large-context models may display minor score variance; we include a model regression check during the pilot to validate quality.

If helpful, Stephanie can add a recommended ramp schedule tuned to your expected token volume and burst patterns.

—Ben

Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity options & sizing — internal ramp recommendation

Internal note (not to be sent externally yet):
Based on PulseCare's traffic profile (CSV attached), recommended activation for Option B:
- Week 0–2: 32 GPUs online, but reserve commit to 8 GPUs billed (warmup/testing)
- Week 3–6: Activate up to 20 GPUs (A/B traffic shift to measure latency under load)
- Week 7–12: Full 32 GPUs active, enable burst windows (evenings 6–10pm PST)
- Include prefix caching and model parallelism tuning in week 1 to reduce token costs by ~18% after warmup.

Suggest approving a one-time 15% introductory credit on committed capacity for first 3 months to shorten sales cycle.

—Stephanie
